title: Day 2 Knowledge Check: Dense Embeddings & Qdrant Filtering

questions.question: Why combine Qdrant metadata payload filters (e.g., category='database') with cosine vector search?

options.A: To deterministically exclude runbooks from unrelated subsystems before ranking similarity.
options.B: Because cosine similarity cannot work on text longer than 10 words.
options.C: To compress Hugging Face model weights on disk.

questions.explanation: Metadata filters act as a deterministic guardrail so database alerts never match networking SOPs.
questions.implication: Without payload filtering, high-level words like 'timeout' or 'exhausted' cause cross-service false positives during P1 outages.

questions.question: Why does UseCaseLoader assign a distinct Qdrant collection_name per domain?

options.A: To prevent cross-domain vector bleed when switching between SRE, CI/CD, and Payment Ops.
options.B: Because Qdrant only allows 10 vectors per collection.

questions.explanation: Isolating collections (e.g., sre_runbooks vs cicd_runbooks) keeps domain knowledge cleanly separated.
questions.implication: Multi-tenant or multi-domain knowledge bases require collection or tenant-ID isolation to guarantee data governance and retrieval precision.

questions.question: Why normalize dense embedding vectors to unit length (L2 norm = 1)?

options.A: So dot-product computation equals exact cosine similarity.
options.B: To convert float32 vectors into JSON strings.

questions.explanation: For unit-normalized vectors, dot product and cosine similarity are mathematically identical.
questions.implication: Consistent L2 normalization prevents magnitude bias when comparing vectors across different document lengths.
